results.title: 'A lot of anger and a weak government': Why are French public sector workers striking?
results.content: Tens of thousands of people took part in protests across France on Tuesday after unions called a new nationwide public sector strike to demand pay rises. It follows more than a month of unrest and often violent protests led by students that the government has failed to quell. France 24's Marc Perelman explains.

results.title: Deutsche Bank leaks: German lender's dealings with Russian oligarchs under scrutiny
results.content: Germany's finance minister Tuesday urged "full transparency" from Deutsche Bank after international media outlets published reports based on millions of leaked documents that shine a light on questionable past business practices at the banking giant. They include ties to Russian oligarchs, the convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein, and Donald Trump before he became US president. France 24's Douglas Herbert takes a closer look.

results.title: Organisers hoping for 'joyful' demonstration as French public workers strike
results.content: France braced for another day of protests Tuesday as unions called for a nationwide strike by public sector workers in a bid to secure pay rises. Hoping to avoid the violence that has marred recent protests in the country, organisers were hoping for a "joyous and festive" occasion, reports France 24's Claire Paccalin from a march in Paris.

results.title: Shenzhen: Inside ‘China’s Silicon Valley’
results.content: When Xi Jinping hosts Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin at this year's APEC summit, he'll be doing it in one of his country's most technologically advanced cities. Shenzhen is China's premier hub for cutting-edge tech – a place where robo-taxis and AI-powered drones are a normal part of the background... Its current status is the result of decades of policies aimed at opening up the once communist country to international markets and foreign investment.

results.title: Deutsche Bank shares drop after reports exposing Epstein payments, Russia dealings
results.content: Deutsche Bank shares fell more than 6% Tuesday after media reports based on leaked documents detailed the bank's dealings with clients including Russian oligarchs, US President Donald Trump and the late financier Jeffrey Epstein.

results.title: Serbia's student-backed MPs take seats in parliament after election win
results.content: Serbia's Student ⁠List lawmakers entered parliament ​on Tuesday, cheered on by hundreds of supporters, after their October ​election victory ended 14 years of rule by the Serbian Progressive Party (SNS). The Student List, a group that includes academics, professionals, farmers, actors and activists ​chosen ‌by student assemblies, secured 140 seats in the ⁠250-member parliament in October 25 polls, while the SNS gained 104.

results.title: Trump says he takes possible Iran bomb threat to Washington 'very seriously'
results.content: President Donald Trump said Tuesday that US authorities take any possible threats to Washington ‘very seriously’, following reports that Iran was planning to target senior Trump administration officials, possibly with a radioactive bomb. Tehran dismissed the reports as ‘fabricated’.

results.title: Urban Zulu and '100 Reasons to Stay Single in Lagos': Telling African stories on their own terms
results.content: Africa's creative industries are attracting growing international attention, from fashion and film to television and music. But as African stories reach audiences around the world, a bigger question is emerging: who gets to tell those stories, and who gets to shape how the continent is seen? At FAME Week Africa in Cape Town, arts24 met some of the creatives driving that conversation.

results.title: France's Le Pen promises to lower retirement age if she wins election
results.content: French far-right ​leader Marine Le ​Pen vowed on Tuesday to repeal President ​Emmanuel ‌Macron's pension ⁠reform if she is ‌elected next spring and ⁠bring down the retirement age to ​60 to 62. She ‌also set out plans to ‌create a fund worth €900 ​billion ($990.54 billion) to help pay for pensions in ​the long term. It ​would take a generation ​to build up the fund, she added.

results.title: France hit by fresh nationwide public sector strike
results.content: Demonstrators gathered across France on Tuesday after unions called a nationwide strike by public sector workers in a bid to secure pay rises, despite government efforts to ease tensions as demonstrations roil the country.

results.title: Calls for cooperation as ASEAN summit awaits Trump
results.content: The twice-yearly ASEAN summit of Southeast Asian nations is underway, with major global powers also descending upon the Philippines. It is a crucial moment for the region, as ASEAN leaders look to strengthen their influence and collaboration in an increasingly divided global landscape. The arrival of US President Donald Trump on Tuesday is also being welcomed as well as protested, as Charli James reports.

results.title: Estonia closes its border with Russia but can it keep Moscow out?
results.content: Estonia announced this weekend it would close its border with Russia, after blaming its eastern neighbour of attempting to sabotage one of its drone factories. But at a time when the internet has become one of Russia’s most potent weapons to wage hybrid warfare, does closing the border even matter?

results.title: 'We're kind of at a stalemate': French government and unions 'dancing around each other'
results.content: Amid continuing protests in France and tense negotiations between the government and trade unions, Delano D'Souza is pleased to welcome Paul Smith, Associate Professor in French and Francophone Studies at the University of Nottingham. “What's happening is that there are two parties kind of dancing around each other.” Smith explains that the government wants to delay negotiations until after trade union elections on 10 December, while the unions want an agreement as quickly as possible. With talks “more or less broken down” over a two-point difference in public sector pay proposals, he describes the situation as “kind of at a stalemate.”

results.title: Did the US use ‘blackout bombs’ in Iran? Images reveal mysterious fibres at infrastructure sites
results.content: Photographs published by Iranian local media suggest that US forces may have used graphite bombs, also known as ‘blackout bombs’, against infrastructure in Iran in recent days. These weapons are designed to disrupt electricity supplies by causing short circuits rather than physically destroying power facilities.

results.title: French far-right candidate Le Pen vows to end Macron's pension reform if elected
results.content: Far-right French presidential contender Marine Le Pen said Tuesday she would eliminate President Emmanuel Macron's pension reform, allowing hundreds of thousands of French workers to retire earlier, and create a new €900 billion retirement fund. The frontrunner in polls to win the presidential race is seeking to convince investors she can balance one of her most popular pledges with promises ​to restore order to ‌the public finances.

results.title: Singer-songwriter Mélissa Laveaux: 'Women need more positions of power in the music industry'
results.content: One of France's top musical artists has spoken to FRANCE 24 about the need to empower more women in music. Mélissa Laveaux is currently taking part in the "Les Femmes s'en mêlent" or "Women get involved" festival, which is holding a series of events across the country in an initiative that started nearly 30 years ago and is still going today. The aim is to address the underrepresentation of female artists at music festivals. She spoke to us in Perspective.

results.title: Ukraine: Two bridges in Kyiv heavily damaged by Russian strikes
results.content: Russia hit two major bridges in Kyiv while Ukraine struck Moscow's link to annexed Crimea for the second night in a row, officials said Tuesday, ahead of a historic meeting of Chinese, US and Russian leaders. Detals from the ground by FRANCE 24 correspondent in Kyiv, Gulliver Cragg.

results.title: Ukraine strikes major Russian bridge in Crimea with drones and missiles
results.content: Ukrainian drones and missiles struck a vital bridge linking Russia to the occupied Crimean Peninsula, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said Tuesday, calling it an “unprecedented” operation as Russia reported that its forces downed a record number of Ukrainian drones for the second straight day. Meanwhile, Russia struck two major bridges in Kyiv.

results.title: Ukraine, Russia hit key bridges ahead of Putin-Xi-Trump summit
results.content: Ukraine struck Russia's Crimean bridge for the second night in a row on Tuesday, shutting it down, while Russia hit two major bridges in Kyiv -- the latest wave of attacks that come ahead of a historic meeting of the Chinese, US and Russian leaders.

results.title: Two Marseille drug traffickers sentenced to life in prison over triple murder
results.content: Two figures in Marseille’s drug trafficking ring were sentenced to life in prison on Monday over a triple murder committed in 2020. Among the victims was Brahim Chabane, the older brother of anti-drug activist and deputy mayor of Marseille Amine Kessaci.

results.title: 'Weirdo specialist' is the new Bond: Papers react to Robert Pattinson as 007
results.content: PRESS REVIEW – Tuesday, November 17: European papers react to five EU countries' plan for a migrant expulsion centre in Rwanda. In other news, the Guardian reveals Israel's use of Amazon's cloud system for facial recognition in Gaza. Plus: the wait for the new James Bond is finally over.

results.title: French presidential debate: 'Le Pen exposed xenophobic and authoritarian aspects of her policies'
results.content: Eve Irvine is pleased to welcome Damien Lecomte, French political scientist, researcher, and lecturer at the University of Paris 1 Panthéon-Sorbonne. With five months to go before France's presidential election, Marine Le Pen leads the opinion polls, while Jean-Luc Mélenchon emerges as her most likely second-round opponent. Lecomte says that "the other candidates are basically fighting for the second spot" and that the center and right are "desperately trying to find a way to avoid a second round" between the two. He also warns that a Le Pen presidency could "really change the political life with more xenophobic and nationalistic policies,"even if her ability to secure a parliamentary majority remains uncertain.

results.title: COP31: Corporate interests gain access to govt delegations participating in climate negotiations
results.content: Eve Irvine is pleased to welcome Siphesihle Mvundla, South African Climate and Energy Justice Campaigner at groundWork, a non-profit environmental justice organization. At COP31 in Turkey, representatives of major polluting industries have gained access to climate negotiations through government delegations, accredited organisations and other participation arrangements, according to research by the Kick Big Polluters Out coalition. Mvundla questions the extent of their involvement: "This year particularly, it's not just about the numbers, but it's about the influence that these private interests would have on the negotiations."
